issue.title: test_agents_help_renders_sorted_subcommands flakes under the full parallel lane across three workspaces

task_type_fields.evidence:
Promoted by `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` as a reproducible flake over the durable host record store, on 4 gate-eligible (<=5-failure) full-run records spanning 3 independent workspaces and 3 days:

- 20260823T132245Z-e2056bddebf0 (4 failures)
- 20260823T133057Z-dcbf570d53a3 (3 failures)
- 20260825T142323Z-70a9d101583f (4 failures)
- 20260825T151728Z-9fb3a1805e3c (5 failures)

The spread across unrelated workspaces and change sets is what the gate's evidence bar keys on: the failures share no common changed file, and independent passing runs interleave them.

PASSES SERIALLY on master f56cf4333: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/main/test_parser_command_help.py::test_agents_help_renders_sorted_subcommands` gives `passed` in 0.01s. It also passed in the full 37073-node check-full run driven from this workspace (monitor hxz0b4zxzgcw).

A 0.01s node that only fails under the parallel lane suggests shared process-global parser/subcommand registry state rather than a timing bound -- plausibly the same class sase-j7 ("Fix the sase-ct flake class at its root - process-global state leaking between tests") is chartered against. The worker should check that epic before treating this as an isolated node.

Reported by epic sase-tt's land agent (sase-tt.land) while triaging the flake gate before closing sase-tt. Not caused by that epic: the earliest records predate it by two days.

payload.description: A 0.01s node that only fails under the parallel lane points at shared process-global parser/subcommand registry state, which is the leak class this epic is chartered to fix at its root.
